toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Short answer: this is not a group-wide problem. It is concentrated in the eleven associates staffed on Kestrel: eight have resigned, against one of the thirteen other associates in the group, a normal rate. Pay, the firm-wide hours target and general market movement apply equally to those thirteen and to other groups, so they don't explain the spike. I'm fairly confident of that.

What I can't tell you is whether the driver is the Kestrel workload or how the work is supervised. All eleven are recorded under Dorian Faulk, who has associate time on no other matter, so the two overlap completely and no existing record can separate them. Survey comments point to both. Treat blaming either as a guess for now.

Next steps: don't announce the £12k payment or close the review; it targets a cause the evidence doesn't support and ends the inquiry. Approve the £9k confidential interviews now, run by someone outside the group and designed to separate workload from supervision. Hold the £160k contract reviewers and any change of supervisor until those results arrive, about three weeks. Meanwhile, record matter and supervising partner in attrition reporting.
output.methodChoice: Compared leavers by matter and supervising partner within the group (X13). Stopped after one item: the other catalogue items cannot separate two explanations that overlap completely; only structured confidential interviews can.
